audit.whatIsWrong: phases[].side was "Skill" on all seven rows while the packet chart and content win[] both read Neeko on all seven.
audit.why: Winds of War is a slow 11s poke at 825 range, Justice Punch reaches only 650, and Shield of Durand soaks rather than answers. Neeko roots at 1000 and blooms at 800, and Galio's scaling is utility, not duel damage — so no stage of the lane flips to him.
audit.corrected: All seven sides moved to Neeko with each why rewritten from the template into a Galio-specific reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes named Luden's as the thing that matters and never mentioned that Galio's level 6 is a roam, not a duel spike.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140 with a 4000-5500 range: it is a map tool. Nothing in his kit spikes the 1v1.
audit.corrected: Level 3 root-bloom is the kill pattern; level 6 is his roam, not a duel; items barely move it.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit (defect item 3) and described Justice Punch only as "his dash knockup".
audit.why: The numbers that decide this lane: Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7 at 650 range and his only engage; Shield of Durand 18/17/16/15/14 with a taunt at 275 range; Winds of War 11s at rank 1; Hero's Entrance 180s at rank 1. Neeko's E is 12s at 1000 range, so she out-ranges the engage and can root the charge before it arrives.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1 and reaches only 650 — step up when it is spent; trade after Shield of Durand, never into the 275-range taunt.

audit.whatIsWrong: The most punishable cooldown was named but never quantified.
audit.why: A spent Justice Punch leaves him with no way to reach you for 11 seconds at rank 1; that is the entire green light in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Numbers added for Justice Punch, Shield of Durand and Hero's Entrance.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the full layer said that Galio's real value is leaving the lane, even though the content layer says it three times.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance reaches 4000-5500 units and is 180s at rank 1 — shoving the wave taxes every use of it.
audit.corrected: Wave and carry advice rewritten around making a roam cost him the wave.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed (defect item 2): dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim under a title about cloning the disengage, dontsFull[1].d was the generic clone paragraph under a title about saving E, and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under a title about extended trades.
audit.why: Each title promised one thing and the body explained another.
audit.corrected: All three replaced with Galio-grounded content matching their titles.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - W Shapesplitter clone spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: Track Galio’s Justice Punch: His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Justice Punch: 11s at rank 1, 650 range. It is his only engage, so a spent one is a free window to step up.

edits.before: Poke blooms and tell lies — your trades are even and your information war isn't. Every clone he answers wrong is tempo.
edits.after: Winds of War is slow and sidesteppable: walk up on every cast, trade autos into Q, and bait Shield of Durand before you commit.

edits.before: Post-6, hunt clumps: disguise into the wave, R the river contest, root the scatter. One good crouch is a won objective.
edits.after: When he channels Hero's Entrance to leave, shove the wave and either match the roam or take the plate he just paid you for.

edits.before: Best wave: a bloom-cleared push that crashes while your clone walks somewhere worth lying about — every shove is also a misdirection. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.
edits.after: Best wave: constantly pushing — a Galio who leaves on Hero's Entrance hands the whole wave to your tower. Worst wave: frozen at his tower with your E down, where a 650-range Justice Punch into the taunt starts a fight you cannot walk out of. Crash timing: crash before his R comes up, so following him costs you nothing at all.

edits.after: If Galio gets a kill his roams start paying — shove harder, ping the side lanes whenever Hero's Entrance is off its 180s cooldown, and hold E strictly for the Justice Punch charge rather than poking with it.

edits.before: Carry through deception — every fight you start disguised begins 5v4 in spirit; your job is the patience the crouch demands.
edits.after: Carry by taxing his map: every wave you shove makes a 180s Hero's Entrance cost him farm, and the lane damage is already yours.

edits.before: You are the ambush their comp can't draft against: disguise, flank, Pop Blossom on three, root the survivors. The clone scouts the setup for free.
edits.after: His threat is R ganks and teamfight taunts, not the duel — track the roams, hold Pop Blossom for the clump he lands on, and out-farm him.

edits.before: Galio spends Justice Punch early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.

edits.before: The clone is your scout, your fake, and your escape — spending it on idle tricks near assassin timers is how Neekos get audited.
edits.after: His only engage is one 11s charge — bank E for it, but a root you never cast is just a kill window handed back to him.

edits.before: Q-poking with E banked 'for safety' until the lane forgets your kill threat exists — the root IS the threat; the bloom is just the receipt.
edits.after: Once the root ends, Shield of Durand taunts at 275 range, and every extra second you stand next to him belongs entirely to Galio.

notes: Chart: full layer said Skill on all seven rows while packet and content both said Neeko; moved as one group with rewritten whys. diff stays EVEN and diffRating 5.5/10 — the win rate is 52.84% over 176 games, which does not justify moving them.
